newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigeria's AP wants Chevron field.
newsitem.headline: Nigeria's AP wants Chevron field.

text.p: Nigerian oil products marketing company African Petroleum Plc (AP) said on Tuesday it was awaiting official approval to take over a small Chevron Nigeria oilfield.
"We've concluded discussions with Chevron for acquisition of the oilfield and are only waiting for the approval of the oil minister," company spokesman Segun Adeleke said.

AP, one of the main oil products marketers in the country, was British Petroleum in Nigeria until it was nationalised in the late 1970s during a clash between the then military government and Britain over independence for Zimbabwe.
The name was changed to African Petroleum, now owned 40 percent by the Nigerian government and 60 percent by the Nigerian public.
The acquisition will mark the company's re-entry into the upstream sector of the Nigerian oil industry.
The field it wants is called Ajapa on Chevron's Oil Prospecting Licence (OPL) 90 and it is one of the marginal fields acquired by the Nigerian government from major oil-producing companies last year.
The government plans to re-allocate the marginal fields, which the oil majors regard as uneconomic, to indigenous oil operators for exploitation.
"We want the oilfield as part of our diversification strategies," Adeleke said.
He said AP was discussing with U.S. firm Huffco International a joint venture partnership to operate the field.
"The approval from the oil minister would determine our relationship with Huffco," Adeleke said.
